symptom: The first cross-device design put setup instructions, folder configuration, and sync state into a new project-library panel; the existing Nomi page had no clear configuration home or actionable status trigger. During the real canvas continuation journey, deleting one result also removed a physical file still referenced by another result, so the next open was blocked as missing assets.
direct_cause: The implementation rendered sync text directly in project cards and exposed a static mockup panel, while the real settings surface already owned project-location configuration and the sync inspector was called without a persisted expected revision/hash. Result deletion removed its file without checking references from the remaining canvas results.
class_root: Cross-device state and project-owned media lacked single ownership contracts separating configuration (settings), transport (external sync client), readiness (library/open guard), and safe lifecycle cleanup (delete metadata first, delete files only when unreferenced).
affected_population: All users configuring a synced project directory
Users opening a project after another computer changed its manifest
Users with missing assets or an unavailable project folder
entry_points: Project library card and Continue creating action
internal_only_reason: The failure is an internal Nomi information-architecture and state-ownership invariant; no third-party dependency controls the UI trigger.
invariants: Project-directory configuration is rendered only in Settings > File & saving.
Project-library cards never contain sync setup controls; they show only a compact status for folder-backed projects.
An actionable sync warning is emitted only after a comparison against a persisted local baseline revision/hash.
No project is silently overwritten when an external revision is detected.
A physical project asset is deleted only after no remaining canvas result references its project-relative path.
generality_proof: All equivalent user paths converge on the project-location settings component for configuration and the workspace sync inspector for readiness. Persisting a per-device baseline makes revision/hash comparison deterministic whether the external change arrives while Nomi is closed, during focus refresh, or immediately before opening a project.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own the local project-root configuration and communicate that the external sync client, not Nomi, transports files.
Compare the observed manifest and referenced assets with the caller's local baseline and fail closed on invalid state.
Render compact status and open the exception popover/guard without adding a second configuration surface.
Apply result metadata removal first and suppress physical deletion while any remaining result still references the same project asset.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Existing project-location picker already validates directory and writability; the cross-device configuration is added here rather than in the project card.
All project-card actions converge on this component; the card will guard opening with the same inspection result and keep setup out of the card.
The IPC boundary resolves the project root and is the single main-process entry for renderer inspections.
Deletion plans compare the post-removal node graph before returning a physical file target, preventing shared thumbnails or results from becoming missing after reopen.

recurrence.reason: Any new workspace status, provider, or project-card action could repeat the same discoverability and false-status failure if configuration, transport, and readiness are not separated at shared boundaries.
same_class_scan: rg -n 'projectLocation|新项目默认位置|文件与保存' src/workbench/settings electron/settings
Computer Use inspection of the installed Nomi project library and Settings > 文件与保存

prevention.invariant: Every readiness decision compares the observed manifest revision/hash with the per-device baseline and separately checks referenced asset existence.
prevention.failure_mode: Unknown or invalid manifests return an explicit non-ready status; external changes remain actionable and do not auto-overwrite local state.
prevention.strategy: Make the inspector the only source for readiness, pass it through the IPC bridge, and let the settings component own directory configuration while the library owns only presentation and open guarding.

legacy_paths.rationale: The rejected standalone panel is replaced by the approved Settings > File & saving sample; no second configuration surface remains.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The first phase uses user-managed local sync folders and existing Electron/React primitives; no new third-party sync SDK is introduced.

migration: Existing project-location settings remain valid. Existing workspace manifests continue to open; a device with no baseline records its first observed revision as the baseline and only warns on later external changes.
residual_risks: VerySync/Nutstore network transfer itself is outside Nomi's process and still needs a manual two-machine canary before release.
The first device baseline migration must be verified against legacy projects that have no sync-state file.
